title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Closing an Account and Paying Out the Balance
content:
The closure of a Savings & Money Market Accounts product rests with its owner. This page covers how a closure request is registered and confirmed, the charge for closing a young account, how the closing balance is arrived at and paid out, and the state the account is left in.

## Rule

**The owner decides.** The agent registers a closure request, marked as awaiting the customer's confirmation and naming how the balance is to be paid out. The account is closed only once the owner has confirmed that request.

**Overdraft protection link.** Where the account serves as the overdraft protection source of a checking account, the link on that checking account is removed ahead of the closure.

**Early closure fee.** The tier's early closure fee applies to a closure falling inside the early closure window. With the day after opening reckoned as day 1, a closure dated no later than the opening date advanced by the window's count of days bears the fee. The fee is charged as an early closure fee against the balance that is about to be paid out, and it is cut down if necessary so the balance never falls below zero; the balance it is measured against already includes any closing interest the tier pays.

**Accrued interest.** On a tier that pays interest built up since the last cycle close when an account closes, that interest is credited into the closing balance; on other tiers it is not.

**Payout.** The payout is the whole balance that remains once the early closure fee, where due, and the closing interest, where paid, are reflected. It leaves as a single withdrawal, either by internal transfer to a Piedmont Crescent Bank account of the same customer or by an official check mailed to the address on file. The account then stands closed at a zero balance, and any automatic transfer into it is stopped. The payout is never counted against the withdrawal allowance and never attracts an excess withdrawal fee.

## Early closure terms by tier

| Tier | Early closure fee (USD) | Early closure window (calendar days after opening) |
|---|---|---|
| Starter Savings | 0.00 | 90 |
| Statement Savings | 25.00 | 90 |
| Goal Builder Savings | 25.00 | 90 |
| Money Market Account | 25.00 | 90 |
| Premier Money Market | 25.00 | 90 |
| Private Client Money Market | 25.00 | 90 |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical account opened 1 January of a non-leap year)

- Day 90 is 1 April. A closure dated 1 April falls inside the window and the fee applies.
- A closure dated 2 April falls outside it and no early closure fee is charged.

## Illustration (hypothetical Statement Savings closure on day 40)

Assume a balance of 518.00 and a tier that pays no closing interest. The 25.00 early closure fee is charged, the remaining 493.00 is paid out as one withdrawal, and the account closes at zero. Had the balance been only 18.00, the fee would have been cut to 18.00.

## Points of judgement

**Does a closing payout by internal transfer use up one of the cycle's free withdrawals?** No; payouts are outside the allowance entirely.
